operations.label: MALBAC primers; Reverse transcription; Repeat 9x
operations.description: Repeated primer hybridization on RNA and reverse transcription generate multiple first-strand cDNAs. The curved return arrow labeled Repeat 9x connects the RT stage back to the priming region; this local operation represents the depicted repeated cycle without inventing separate sample branches. RNA remains in the resulting RNA/cDNA material.
operations.mechanism: The caption attributes increased RT efficiency and non-polyA transcript detection to primer hybridization at low temperatures, and describes the primer-initiated amplification as quasilinear to reduce amplification bias. These are catalogue schematic claims, not a full-text-verified reaction program.
operations.information_effect: RNA sequence is copied into multiple cDNA products, extending the representation beyond poly(A)-bearing transcripts. Primer-derived segments are retained in the depicted cDNA products.

operations.label: RNA digestion and dC tailing
operations.description: Remove the RNA component and add dC tails to the resulting first-strand cDNAs. The output contains tailed DNA products rather than the preceding RNA/cDNA material. The drawing groups digestion and tailing under one arrow.
operations.mechanism: The C-rich tail creates the complementary priming interface for the subsequent G-enriched primer. The caption states that dC addition to first cDNA strands increases second-strand-synthesis efficiency. No digestion enzyme or tailing enzyme is named in this row.
operations.information_effect: Retains the RNA-derived sequence in DNA and creates a common end interface for second-strand priming.
